title: Metabelian targets stay polynomial with bounded homology
claim: Target: let G be a finite group with an abelian normal subgroup N such that Q = G/N is nilpotent (every metabelian group qualifies, with N = G' or any abelian normal subgroup with abelian quotient). Fix d. Given a finite presentation of a group P with dim H1(P; F_p) <= d for every prime p dividing |Q|, and optionally a bounded number of generators whose images are required to lie in given conjugacy classes, the number of homomorphisms P -> G with those constraints is computable in time polynomial in the size of the presentation: the homomorphisms P -> Q number at most |Q|^d and are enumerated by lifting through a central series of Q with elementary abelian factors, each step a linear system over F_p whose solution space is a translate of Hom(H1(P), F_p^e); and the lifts of each through N are the solutions of a linear system over the finite abelian group N whose coefficients are Fox derivatives evaluated in Z[Q], counted by Smith-normal-form elimination over Z/p^a. This covers closed orientable 3-manifolds with |H1(M; Z)| bounded (presented from triangulations) and knot groups with the meridian class fixed. In contrast S4 is not of this form, and its count on knot groups already sums over the exponentially many homomorphisms to S3 exhibited in BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A.
failure_conditions: A presentation with bounded homology on which the algorithm's count differs from brute-force enumeration for any tested target or class constraint.
More than |Q|^d homomorphisms to Q on a tested presentation, or a lifting step whose solution set is not a translate of the stated space.
An abelian-by-nilpotent decomposition claimed for a group that does not have one (S4 must have none).
foundation_claim_scope: Finitely presented groups with bounded mod-p first homology for the primes dividing |G/N|, including closed 3-manifolds with bounded first homology and knot groups with a fixed meridian class; targets with an abelian normal subgroup and nilpotent quotient. The polynomial-time conversion of a triangulation into a presentation is standard and cited. The statement is a sufficient condition; it does not classify all targets (for example SL(2,3) is not abelian-by-nilpotent). No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library, about 1 s) finds abelian-by-nilpotent decompositions for eight test groups and none for S4, matches brute force on 96 random presentations with bounded mod-p homology (with the bound |Hom(P,Q)| <= |Q|^d) and on 39 knot-group cases with a meridian class, computes the exponential S3 counts 3^n of tripled grid knots with up to 51 generators in hundredths of a second, and passes three controls. No human or external review
